<!-- Generated by Pixl from the skill "Understand the task before you start", version 1. Edit it in the Skills tab, not here: changes made here are overwritten. -->

## Steps
1. Read the task, the story and every acceptance criterion.
2. In your first message write five lines: Goal; Inputs and outputs; Edge cases; Assumptions; Files to read first.
3. Open `docs/knowledge/overview.md` if it exists, then only the files you named.
4. Find how the project runs its tests and write the command down.
5. If something is unclear, pick the most common option, write it under Assumptions and go on. Stop only if the work cannot go on safely.
6. Stop reading when you can name each file you will change.
## Checklist
- [ ] The five lines are written.
- [ ] Each criterion is one sentence a test can check.
- [ ] The test command is known.
## Definition of done
Your first message holds the five lines, and you can name every file you will change.
## Verify
List the project's folder and open the files you named. Run the test command once to see the starting state.
## Common mistakes
- Starting to code before reading anything.
- Inventing requirements the task did not ask for.
- Reading the whole repository: read only what your five lines name.
- Asking a question that has an obvious default.
## Example
Task: "Order totals are wrong." Goal: orders of 100 or more get 10% off. Inputs: a list of prices. Edge cases: exactly 100, empty list. Assumptions: prices are in dollars. Read first: `shop.py`, `tests/test_shop.py`.
